title: Reproducible Implementation & Data
description: Study data versions and splits, experiment manifests and environments, checkpoints and artifact lineage, and implementation validation before scaling. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Data versions and splits
lessons.description: Design a document-level split and duplicate check.
lessons.conceptOverview: Version datasets and split logic, and prevent leakage across train, validation and test partitions. Group related records when needed so near-duplicates do not cross boundaries.
lessons.whyItMatters: Split boundaries should respect related examples.

lessons.title: Experiment manifests and environments
lessons.description: Define a manifest that captures the changed dependency.
lessons.conceptOverview: Record code revision, dependencies, data version, configuration and hardware. A random seed helps but cannot replace the rest of the execution context.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reproducibility requires the complete relevant setup.

lessons.title: Checkpoints and artifact lineage
lessons.description: Create artifact identifiers and provenance links.
lessons.conceptOverview: Track which inputs and configuration produced each checkpoint, metric file and figure. Keep raw results separate from derived summaries so plots can be regenerated and audited.
lessons.whyItMatters: Figures should be traceable to compatible underlying runs.

lessons.title: Implementation validation before scaling
lessons.description: Run a tiny split audit and a controlled overfit check before scaling.
lessons.conceptOverview: Validate small cases, known limits and baseline behavior before expensive runs. Incorrect loss scaling or data handling can invalidate a large experiment while producing plausible curves.
lessons.whyItMatters: Small validation checks can prevent expensive invalid experiments.
